examDifficulty.heading: Is the Media Cloud Accredited Professional Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This page reviews Media Cloud workflows for ad sales, inventory, subscriptions, rights and campaign delivery.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 75 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
66% to pass, which is 40 correct answers out of 60.
Rights & inventory: expect questions on how ad sales, content rights, and subscription entitlements are modeled and enforced in Media Cloud.
Hands-on context matters: candidates who have configured or supported Media Cloud in a real org are better prepared than candidates who only memorize notes.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Review the official objectives and practice distinguishing advertising workflows from subscriptions. For each case, identify the inventory, buyer, audience or billing record the process needs.

examFormat.heading: Media Cloud Accredited Professional Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The Media Cloud Accredited Professional exam is a timed Salesforce credential exam. Use the format below to plan pacing and practice-test strategy.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios describe an advertising or subscription need and ask which record or workflow best represents it.
bestWayToPass: Check content rights first: Match each asset to the licensee, territory, channel, and time period before proposing or selling it.
Confirm ad inventory: Check available placements and capacity before promising airtime or digital space to a client.
Follow the proposal-to-order path: Practice how media plans, proposals, orders, and fulfillment records connect.
Test rights conflicts: Use scenarios with overlapping exclusivity, channels, and dates to see when a booking should be blocked or flagged.

certificationCard.description: This page covers Media Cloud use cases for media companies, including advertising sales, rights and entitlements, campaign delivery and subscription revenue.

keyConcepts.h2: Media Cloud AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Advertising Orders and Inventory
blocks.body: An advertising order can include placements with dates, inventory and prices. Because available airtime or space is limited, check availability before confirming a booking.

blocks.heading: Rights and Entitlements
blocks.body: Rights describe how content may be used, including territory, period and permitted distribution. Keep the entitlement details tied to the content and agreement they govern.

blocks.heading: Revenue and Billing
blocks.body: Media revenue can come from advertising and subscriptions. These models use different customers, terms and billing events, so represent the streams clearly.

blocks.heading: Agencies and Partners
blocks.body: Agencies may buy advertising on behalf of advertisers, while distribution partners may deliver content. Model each party according to its role in the transaction.

blocks.heading: Campaign Delivery and Reporting
blocks.body: Compare booked delivery with actual campaign results. Reports can show pacing and performance; shortfalls may require an agreed make-good or other remedy.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Media Cloud Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Identify whether a scenario concerns advertising inventory, subscriber relationships, rights or revenue.

blocks.heading: Identify the revenue stream
blocks.body: Decide whether the scenario concerns advertising, subscriptions or both before choosing records.

blocks.heading: Treat inventory as limited
blocks.body: Check availability and delivery timing when an advertiser books placements.

blocks.heading: Track rights precisely
blocks.body: Use territory, time period and permitted-use details to determine what distribution is allowed.

blocks.heading: Compare booked and delivered results
blocks.body: Use campaign reporting to identify pacing problems and determine the agreed response.

sampleQuestions.question: A broadcaster sells ad placements and streaming subscriptions. How should the data model treat those revenues?
options: As separate commercial streams with the records each requires
As one product that combines advertising and subscription terms
As two Salesforce orgs in every implementation
sampleQuestions.explanation: Advertising and subscriptions have different buyers, pricing and lifecycles, so model them as distinct commercial streams.
whyWrong: As one product that combines advertising and subscription terms is not the best choice because the scenario calls for As separate commercial streams with the records each requires.
As two Salesforce orgs in every implementation is not the best choice because the scenario calls for As separate commercial streams with the records each requires.
As subscription revenue only is not the best choice because the scenario calls for As separate commercial streams with the records each requires.

sampleQuestions.question: What does an advertising order usually specify?
options: The editorial schedule for every program
One annual charge with no placement details
sampleQuestions.explanation: Order line items describe the placements being purchased, including details such as timing and inventory.
whyWrong: A consumer’s subscription tier is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Campaign placements with timing and inventory details.
The editorial schedule for every program is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Campaign placements with timing and inventory details.
One annual charge with no placement details is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Campaign placements with timing and inventory details.

sampleQuestions.question: Why must available ad inventory be checked before confirming a booking?
options: Regulators require weekly public inventory reports
Airtime and ad space are limited
Advertisers can buy inventory only once
sampleQuestions.explanation: The amount of airtime or space available is finite, so bookings must not exceed it.
whyWrong: Regulators require weekly public inventory reports is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Airtime and ad space are limited.
It determines subscription prices is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Airtime and ad space are limited.
Advertisers can buy inventory only once is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Airtime and ad space are limited.

sampleQuestions.question: A subscriber changes to a lower tier mid-month. How should the billing change be handled?
options: Keep charging the higher tier until the annual term ends
Cancel the subscription and create an unrelated new one
Charge the lower tier retroactively for the full month
Prorate the change over the remaining period
sampleQuestions.explanation: Proration accounts for the time the subscriber had each tier during the billing period.
whyWrong: Keep charging the higher tier until the annual term ends is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Prorate the change over the remaining period.
Cancel the subscription and create an unrelated new one is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Prorate the change over the remaining period.
Charge the lower tier retroactively for the full month is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Prorate the change over the remaining period.

sampleQuestions.question: What does churn measure in a subscription business?
options: The share or rate of subscribers who cancel
Campaign impressions that were not delivered
Repeated programs in a broadcast schedule
sampleQuestions.explanation: Churn tracks subscribers leaving the service over a defined period.
whyWrong: Campaign impressions that were not delivered is not the best choice because the scenario calls for The share or rate of subscribers who cancel.
Unsold advertising inventory is not the best choice because the scenario calls for The share or rate of subscribers who cancel.
Repeated programs in a broadcast schedule is not the best choice because the scenario calls for The share or rate of subscribers who cancel.

sampleQuestions.question: A media company wants to know what content helps retain subscribers. Which information is useful?
options: Press reviews after a program airs
sampleQuestions.explanation: Linking viewing activity to subscriber records helps compare content use with retention.
whyWrong: Advertising prices by time slot is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Viewing behavior linked to subscriber records.
Production budgets alone is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Viewing behavior linked to subscriber records.
Press reviews after a program airs is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Viewing behavior linked to subscriber records.

sampleQuestions.question: What information does an advertising rate card provide?
options: A list of unpaid advertiser invoices
sampleQuestions.explanation: A rate card lists the published prices for the inventory being sold.
whyWrong: The daily order of commercials is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Available consumer subscription tiers.
A list of unpaid advertiser invoices is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Available consumer subscription tiers.
Published prices for advertising inventory is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Available consumer subscription tiers.

sampleQuestions.question: A campaign misses its booked impressions. What remedy may the company offer?
options: Lower the rate card for every advertiser
Cancel all of the advertiser’s future contracts
Offer make-good inventory for the shortfall
sampleQuestions.explanation: A make-good can provide additional inventory to address an agreed delivery shortfall.
whyWrong: Lower the rate card for every advertiser is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Require a second full-price booking.
Cancel all of the advertiser’s future contracts is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Require a second full-price booking.
Offer make-good inventory for the shortfall is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Require a second full-price booking.

sampleQuestions.question: Why represent households as well as individual subscribers?
options: Advertising placements are sold to households
A household subscription may be used by several people
Every household must be recorded by regulation
sampleQuestions.explanation: A shared subscription can cover several viewers, while individual records can represent their separate profiles.
whyWrong: A household subscription may be used by several people is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Advertising placements are sold to households.
Individuals cannot have viewing records is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Advertising placements are sold to households.
Every household must be recorded by regulation is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Advertising placements are sold to households.

sampleQuestions.question: What does yield management seek to do with limited advertising inventory?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Yield management aims to maximize revenue from inventory that has limited availability.
whyWrong: Increase subscribers during a promotion is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Earn the best available revenue from the inventory.
Reduce program production costs is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Earn the best available revenue from the inventory.
Invoice advertisers more quickly is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Earn the best available revenue from the inventory.

sampleQuestions.question: A subscriber’s payment fails. What should a well-designed process do?
options: Ignore the failed payment until renewal
sampleQuestions.explanation: A payment-failure process should follow the configured retry policy and communicate the issue to the subscriber.
whyWrong: Cancel every subscription immediately is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Retry according to policy and notify the subscriber.
Ignore the failed payment until renewal is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Retry according to policy and notify the subscriber.
Delete the subscriber’s account is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Retry according to policy and notify the subscriber.

sampleQuestions.question: How does an advertising agency differ from an advertiser?
options: The agency owns the media company
The agency buys on behalf of advertisers
sampleQuestions.explanation: An agency can place or manage buys on behalf of an advertiser.
whyWrong: The agency owns the media company is not the best choice because the scenario calls for There is no difference in the commercial model.
The agency buys on behalf of advertisers is not the best choice because the scenario calls for There is no difference in the commercial model.
The advertiser represents the broadcaster is not the best choice because the scenario calls for There is no difference in the commercial model.

sampleQuestions.question: Why do media companies bundle subscription content?
options: To eliminate the need to track subscribers
To make all content rights universal
sampleQuestions.explanation: Bundling combines offerings to give subscribers more value and can support retention.
whyWrong: To eliminate the need to track subscribers is not the best choice because the scenario calls for To raise perceived value and support retention.
To make all content rights universal is not the best choice because the scenario calls for To raise perceived value and support retention.
To replace campaign delivery reporting is not the best choice because the scenario calls for To raise perceived value and support retention.

sampleQuestions.question: A campaign targets a particular audience group. What should the booking consider?
options: The billing address of the agency
sampleQuestions.explanation: Targeting depends on matching audience needs with the attributes of available inventory.
whyWrong: Past booking volume alone is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Audience data for the inventory available.
The editorial budget only is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Audience data for the inventory available.
The billing address of the agency is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Audience data for the inventory available.

sampleQuestions.question: Which business area does Media Cloud support?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Media Cloud supports commercial media workflows such as advertising sales and subscriber management.
whyWrong: Only editorial commissioning is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Advertising sales and subscriber management.
Only video streaming technology is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Advertising sales and subscriber management.
Only payroll for media talent is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Advertising sales and subscriber management.
